title: The Caption That Lost the Speaker
premise: A viewer wants to follow a scene without its audio, but the caption shows words with no indication of which offscreen figure spoke. Reviewed speaker identification and meaningful sound labels restore the missing context.
hook: Who said that when neither mouth was on screen?
visible_action: Two offscreen speech paths feed a caption strip; speaker labels attach and a relevant door-sound cue appears.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Captions may need speaker and meaningful sound information as well as spoken words.
gate: Review caption standards and actual audio; do not claim compliance from one example.

editorial_pick.original_reason: Speaker attribution in captions creates a practical accessibility lesson that can be shown directly.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Use two original voices or labeled characters. Compare ambiguous captions with a clearly attributed version.
editorial_pick.gate: Verify caption conventions and readable timing. Do not rely on color alone for speaker identity.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
